doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Streaming, Spotify and funding recordings in Canada versus the U.S.
summary: She dislikes keeping up with new media, criticises Spotify analytics and playlists, and describes grant-funded recordings that are more viable in Canada.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Is it an issue for you to try to keep up with contemporary media? You’re supposed to be an instructor.
It’s like what’s new THIS week.

Actually what I really don’t like, again I guess I’m getting old because I’ve lived through a generation of the heyday of making money off records in jazz. Or not even making money but like clearing a profit. Maybe a small profit, but not going the other way. And now with the gobbling up of our, you know the Maria Schneider whole thing that she’s gone into with the digital world gobbling us up, I totally agree with her. I mean I’m told to have this app on my phone that’s called “Spotify Artist” where I count, and the © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
industry is counting how many people are listening to my music. And they can really see it.
And what do they do with that information?

Well they decide whether or not I’ll get a gig first of all, or they’ll decide whether or not my music is worthy. In their world it has to do with playlists. I mean we never had playlists when I was a kid we made our own playlists. You know? So yeah it’s scary times to say the least. And there’s no money — I mean there is money out there, I have some students that are quite successful with this new platform, like former students that have gone on to really great careers, but I also have a huge swath of musicians that are not even willing to record at a high level because what’s the point? It costs so much. It’s this infernal machine.
Have you self-financed some of your recordings over the last ten years or so?

I’m in the middle of one right now. I have, mostly through grant funding. Although I have to say the last small album I did was the first time in a long time where I went into the studio and the label paid me, they paid my musicians and they paid for all of the production and they still printed CDs. They had grants to do that mind you. But that’s also a very big difference between Canada and the U.S.
That it’s still happening in Canada?

Yeah, there’s still a lot of media funding that was, you know, that laws were put into place. It’s like if you’re going to go and destroy us you better have a bit of funding left to prop up the industry that once was, or for us to continue in it otherwise not much is going to happen with art.
